- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 74496c64b0637103f87cceec3f37932a48813e65` → `packageMentionDocs`.

```sh

git fetch origin 7560ce704adfd5656edf593ae5c510ae4a2565c0 && git checkout 7560ce704adfd5656edf593ae5c510ae4a2565c0

git fetch origin 74496c64b0637103f87cceec3f37932a48813e65 b5a3141e7f0a2efdf94e9ae94b88d935cf96f37a && git checkout -B drift-repro 74496c64b0637103f87cceec3f37932a48813e65 && git merge --no-ff b5a3141e7f0a2efdf94e9ae94b88d935cf96f37a
```

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than

> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 74496c64b0637103f87cceec3f37932a48813e65` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b5a3141e7f0a2efdf94e9ae94b88d935cf96f37a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/rest/src/import-prepare.ts, packages/rest/src/import-inline-mapping-entry.test.ts + packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-mapping.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/rest/src/import-mapping.ts, packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx, content/docs/references/api/export.mdx, content/docs/references/api/error-code-ledger.mdx, .changeset/25078-csv-text-cell.md

Every derived gate family the diff reaches is green on the head, the Governed Surface Queue Guard included.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, read in the cited code:

1. **Inline `FieldMappingEntry.transform` ∈ {trim, uppercase, lowercase} is now applied per string cell — RIGHT.** `FieldMappingEntrySchema` (`packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts`) declares the enum with `.describe('Transformation to apply during mapping')`; `ImportMappingSchema` admits the array form on `ImportRequestSchema.mapping`; on `main` the parser kept `mapping[e.sourceField] = e.targetField` and nothing else, so the card's declared-but-dropped defect is real. The dev's "implemented nowhere" measurement holds: `git grep` for `case 'uppercase'|'lowercase'|'trim'|'date_format'` across `packages` (tests and spec excluded) returns nothing, and no consumer of `ExportImportTemplate` exists outside spec, so there was no shared implementation to reuse and the PR adds exactly one table (`INLINE_TRANSFORMS`). Applied after the rows are built and the `maxRows` ceiling, before `metaMap`/coercion: the right seam, and `trimWhitespace` (default on) still trims downstream, so `trim` only matters when the request turns it off — the test pins that case.
2. **`none` and `lookup` copy the cell — RIGHT.** Matches the named path's `case 'none': case 'lookup'` in core `applyMappingToRows` (lookup resolved downstream by `metaMap` reference resolution). A plain entry or `transform: 'none'` with no default and not required yields no rule, so the row is built exactly as before — the control test pins the byte-identical rename.
3. **`defaultValue` fills a blank cell, blank judged by core `isBlank(value, nullValues)` — RIGHT.** `isBlank` is the predicate `import-coerce.ts` uses and is exported from core's index (`export * from './utils/import-coerce.js'`); `@objectstack/core` is already a `workspace:*` dependency of rest and already imported by five rest sources. Missing column (no header named `sourceField`) is handled: `row[targetField]` is `undefined` → blank → default written. `null` as a default writes `null` (`hasDefault` is `!== undefined`), which is the only coherent reading.
4. **`required: true` with a still-blank cell refuses the whole request `400 MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` before any row, dry run and commit alike — RIGHT as a contract, with the row-vs-request choice judged under ③.** Code and status: `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` is in the error-code ledger (`error-code-ledger.mdx` line 212) and the ledger fixes it at 400 with the single `controlled_by_parent` 422 exception, which this is not. The refusal's row numbers are `i + 1` over the built rows; the runner numbers its report `const rowNo = i + 1` over the same array (`import-runner.ts` line 1115), so the refusal and the per-row report agree. Both REST doors answer `res.status(prep.status).json({ code, error })` — the same envelope every other `prepareImportRequest` refusal uses; the test's `error?.code ?? code` reads it correctly.
5. **`date_format` (and any name outside the table) refuses `400 UNSUPPORTED_TRANSFORM` — RIGHT.** Same code, same door, same precedent as the named mapping's declared-but-refused `javascript` (core `applyMappingToRows` default arm; documented in `import-mappings.mdx` lines 129 and 221). `FieldMappingEntry` carries no format argument, so the transform has no defined input; Prime Directive #10 allows "reject loudly" over "declare and skip". The spec enum is left as is: the same `FieldMappingEntrySchema` serves `ExportImportTemplateSchema` in both directions, so trimming `date_format` there is a wider spec decision, correctly out of this card. The accept-set narrows exactly as declared: two request shapes that ran on `main` now 400.
6. **Reach of the narrowing — WRONG as stated.** The PR body and changeset say the rules run "for both doors that parse through this function (the sync import and the async import job)". `prepareImportRequest` has THREE non-test callers on `main`: `data-action-routes.ts` lines 369 and 483 (the two named) and `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.ts` line 550, which spreads `...body` into the parser so an inline `mapping` array reaches it unchanged. The repository's own precedent for this parser names all three (`.changeset/25078-csv-text-cell.md`: "the sync import …, the async import job … and plugin-auth's admin user import (`POST /api/v1/auth/admin/import-users`), with an inline mapping or a named one"). The behaviour at that third door is the same and correct (it answers `fail(prep.status, prep.code, prep.error)`), and plugin-auth's own code is untouched so no changeset on it is owed — but a BREAKING entry that ships as the `@objectstack/rest` CHANGELOG must name every door it narrows, and a released entry can only be corrected by a dedicated docs-only PR afterwards. Fix: name the third door in the changeset body and the PR body's `Clause-②` sentence.
7. **Documented contract on the inline form — WRONG, left stale.** `content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx` (hand-written tree, editable in a code PR) states in its "Inline `mapping` vs `mappingName`" table: `Transforms | None — rename only` for the inline form (line 202), and its "Rejections before any row is read" table (lines 212–223: "whole-request failures — nothing is written, and there is no per-row report") lists `UNSUPPORTED_TRANSFORM` only for the artifact's `javascript` and does not list `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` at all. After this diff the inline form carries transforms, defaults and a required rule, and two new whole-request refusals exist. The page now contradicts the shipped contract in the one place an operator looks. The dev's report said "no file outside packages/rest" and flagged only the `import-mapping.ts` docblock; this page was not noticed. The `references/api/export.mdx` rows are auto-generated from the unchanged spec and stay correct. Fix: update the two tables on that page (and, since the package is already being edited, the `import-mapping.ts` seam docblock "inline = a plain … RENAME" that the dev deferred).
8. **No other surface moves.** No `packages/spec` change (the `TypeScript Type Check` artifact gates are green), no new export from rest (`InlineEntryRule`, `INLINE_TRANSFORMS`, `readInlineEntryRule`, `applyInlineEntryRules` are module-private), the compact `{ column: field }` record and the named `mappingName` path (mutually exclusive via `CONFLICTING_MAPPING`, so the new block never runs beside `applyMappingToRows`) are untouched, the client SDK's `import(object, request: ImportRequest)` types are unchanged. In-repo senders of an inline entry with a `transform`: none outside spec and tests (`git grep` over client, cli, console, plugins, docs, examples) — so no in-repo caller is broken by the narrowing.
9. **Tests — RIGHT.** Route-level through the real `POST /api/v1/data/:object/import` handler on sqlite `:memory:`, eight cases covering the card's reproduction, the email-merge case, `trim` under `trimWhitespace: false`, default for blank cell and missing column, required refusal on dry run and commit with zero rows written, required satisfied by default, `date_format` refusal, and the plain-entry control. The ablation report (guard flipped → 5 of 8 red, the 3 parse-time/control cases green) is consistent with the code paths each case exercises.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25491-import-inline-mapping-entry-rules.md`: `'@objectstack/rest': patch`, title `fix(rest)!:`, `**BREAKING**` banner with Before / Now / Fix, exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, and both declaration lines present line-initial on the changeset AND the PR body: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`.

Judged against the rule: the kind is `none` (nothing a metadata author writes changes — a REST request body's handling moves, no spec key, authorable spelling or stored shape), so the level is **patch**; a non-protocol change that is breaking "ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition" — which this changeset does. `(narrowing)` is the right arm: two accepted request shapes are now refused, nothing is widened. The only package the diff moves is `@objectstack/rest`; `plugin-auth` inherits the behaviour through its workspace dependency with no source change, so no second changeset is owed. `Check Changeset`, `check-adr-0087-registration` and the queue guard are green on the head. **Level, arm and kind: right.** The body's prose defect is ①-6 (reach), not the level.

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (os-dev-report 6374589262, `deviations`; `open_questions` is empty):

- **`date_format` refused `400 UNSUPPORTED_TRANSFORM` rather than implemented — ANSWERED, accepted.** No format argument exists on the entry; the card's own "Expected" offered a clear refusal as an acceptable outcome; the `javascript` precedent in the same pipeline is the same shape (declared by spec, refused loudly at the door). The spec enum stays because it also serves export templates; whether to trim or parameterise `date_format` on `FieldMappingEntry` is a spec question outside this card — not filed here, since the loud refusal means nothing is faked (Prime Directive #10 corollary satisfied).
- **A `required` miss refuses the whole request rather than failing the row — ANSWERED, accepted with the reasoning recorded.** The reason given (the core runner has no pre-failed-row seam; core is outside the file surface) is true on `main`: `runImport` builds `results[i]` itself from coercion and write outcomes and takes no caller-supplied failures. Whole-request refusal is the shape every other mapping-level verdict in this parser takes (`refuseUnknownMappingTargets`, `CONFLICTING_MAPPING`), it names every offending row so one edit fixes the file, it runs on the dry run too so the preview still reports it, and nothing is written. A per-row variant would be a core change under its own card; the dev noted it in Acceptance notes, which is the right carrier.
- **Clause-② moved from `no` to `no (narrowing)`, `!` title, patch + BREAKING — ANSWERED, right (see ②).**
- **Repo-wide `pnpm lint` not run locally, narrowed to the two files — ANSWERED:** `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Lint · ESLint` are green on the head; the local gap is closed by CI.
- **PR body opens with the dispatch-mandated HTML attribution comment — ANSWERED:** a platform marker the dispatch requires; it is not part of the contract under review.
- **Out-of-scope note: `import-mapping.ts` docblock calls the inline mapping a plain rename — ESCALATED to a fix in this PR** together with the docs page it mirrors (①-7): the seam description is in the package this PR already edits, and the hand-written docs page that restates the same rule is the one the hunks falsify.

Not flagged by the dev, found here: ①-6 (the third door the narrowing reaches is unnamed) and ①-7 (the inline-vs-named docs table and the pre-row refusal table are now false). Both are prose on public surfaces (the CHANGELOG-bound changeset and the operator-facing docs page), both are small, and both must be corrected on the head before this narrowing lands.

**What lifts the verdict:** (a) changeset body and PR `Clause-②` sentence name `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/import-users` (plugin-auth) beside the two REST doors; (b) `content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx` — inline column of the comparison table says the entry form carries `transform` (trim / uppercase / lowercase; none / lookup copy), `defaultValue` and `required`, and the pre-row refusal table gains the inline `date_format` (and undeclared-name) cause under `UNSUPPORTED_TRANSFORM` plus a `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` row; (c) the `packages/rest/src/import-mapping.ts` seam docblock stops calling the inline form a plain rename. No code change is asked for.
